newsitem.title: USA: More Mississippi locks may close if water rises.
newsitem.headline: More Mississippi locks may close if water rises.

text.p: More locks along the Mississippi River may be shut down to navigation if river levels continue to rise, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.
"Lock and Dam 18 at Gladstone, Ill., is still open but may close if water levels rise further," said Bob Hildebrand, chief warrant officer, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office at St Louis.
Locks and Dams 19 at Keokuk, Iowa and Lock 20 at Canton, Mo., were in the same situation. "Locks 18 through 27, near St Louis, are being watched and evaluated by the Lockmasters," Hildebrand said.
The high water on the Mississippi resulted from snow melt after above-average snow hit the Dakotas and Minnesota last winter, river officials said.

The Coast Guard said all locks and dams from upper and lower St. Anthony Falls, Minn., south to Lock and Dam 17, New Boston, Ill., remained closed except for Lock and Dam 7 at LaCrescent, Minn., which reopened on Wednesday.
The Coast Guard also said a total of 24 towing vessels, southbound, cannot travel downriver and 12 vessels northbound.
"They can move but they are more or less stuck between the locks. But barge traffic remains light," Hildebrand said.

River levels were slowly falling in upper reaches of the Mississippi River. The river at Minneapolis was at 13.8 feet, below the 16-foot flood stage and down 0.6 feet from Wednesday and was still dropping, the Coast Guard said.
At St Paul, Minn., the river stood at 20.57 feet, above the 14-foot flood stage, but was slowly receding. It crested on Wednesday.
At Davenport, Iowa, Mississippi River levels were at 18.6 feet, 3.6 feet above flood stage of 15 feet. But the crest was still not determined, he said.

Also, the river at St Louis stood at 30.4 feet, up slightly from Wednesday's 29.2 feet and just above flood stage at 30 feet, Hildebrand said. It was expected to crest on Thursday at 31 feet, the Coast Guard said.
The safety zone for the St Louis harbor set on April 14 was still in effect.
Elsewhere, rising water on the Missouri River prompted the Guard to set a no-wake zone early this week from Waverly, Mo. to St Charles, Mo., near St Louis.
"The entire Missouri River has crested as of Wednesday" but regarding Kansas City, Kan., levels were at 25.19 feet, well below flood stage of 32 feet and still dropping, Hildebrand said.
The Missouri River at St Charles crested on Wednesday at 28.3 feet up from the 24-foot flood stage.
Weather remained the key. If there is heavy rain in conjuction with further rapid snow melt, then water levels could again rise everywhere along the Missouri, Hildebrand said.
